# VS Code Keyboard Shortcuts for XSL Development

## Testing & Debugging

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Test current XSL file | `F5` | `F5` |
| Run Task | `Ctrl+Shift+P` → "Run Task" | `Cmd+Shift+P` → "Run Task" |
| Open Debug Panel | `Ctrl+Shift+D` | `Cmd+Shift+D` |
| Toggle Terminal | `` Ctrl+` `` | `` Cmd+` `` |

## XML/XSL Editing

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Format Document | `Shift+Alt+F` | `Shift+Option+F` |
| Go to Symbol | `Ctrl+Shift+O` | `Cmd+Shift+O` |
| Find All References | `Shift+F12` | `Shift+F12` |
| Rename Symbol | `F2` | `F2` |
| Toggle Comment | `Ctrl+/` | `Cmd+/` |
| Fold All | `Ctrl+K Ctrl+0` | `Cmd+K Cmd+0` |
| Unfold All | `Ctrl+K Ctrl+J` | `Cmd+K Cmd+J` |

## Navigation

| Action | Windows/Linux | Mac |
|--------|---------------|-----|
| Go to File | `Ctrl+P` | `Cmd+P` |
| Go to Line | `Ctrl+G` | `Cmd+G` |
| Search in Files | `Ctrl+Shift+F` | `Cmd+Shift+F` |
| Go Back | `Alt+Left` | `Ctrl+-` |
| Go Forward | `Alt+Right` | `Ctrl+Shift+-` |
| Quick Open (Recent) | `Ctrl+R` | `Cmd+R` |

## Custom Tasks (via Ctrl+Shift+P → Run Task)

- **Test Current XSL View** - Validates and tests the open XSL file
- **Test Tech Product Browser** - Tests the tech product browser specifically
- **Validate All User XSL Views** - Tests all XSL files in user/ directory
- **Open Test Output in Browser** - Opens test_output.html
- **Create New Custom View** - Scaffolds a new XSL view from template

## Quick Commands

Type these in Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P`):

```
> XML: Format
> Run Task
> Debug: Start Debugging
> File: Compare Active File With...
```

## Pro Tips

1. **Multi-cursor editing**: `Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down` (Windows) or `Option+Cmd+Up/Down` (Mac)
2. **Duplicate line**: `Shift+Alt+Down` (Windows) or `Shift+Option+Down` (Mac)
3. **Move line**: `Alt+Up/Down` (Windows) or `Option+Up/Down` (Mac)
4. **Select word**: `Ctrl+D` (Windows) or `Cmd+D` (Mac) - press repeatedly for multi-select
5. **Zen Mode**: `Ctrl+K Z` (Windows) or `Cmd+K Z` (Mac) - distraction-free editing
